summary: A red pole light of 1884 on Lennox Passage, Isle Madame; a wooden tower from about 1907, automated in 1961, today a seasonal green flash.

structures.note: 1908 report: square in plan, 32 ft (9.8 m) from base to top of lantern ventilator (cite 2); 1909 changed-lights list says a 25-foot tower (cite 3); Lighthouse Directory gives 8.5 m (28 ft) (cite 9). The Coast Guard list gives a 9.2 m focal height and no tower height.

access.note: Grounds open; tower closed. Reached by a gravel road inside Lennox Passage Provincial Park.

events.note: Three pole lights established along Lennox Passage; the Grandique Point light was fixed red, shown from a lantern on a mast
Mast and shed moved to a safer position (LighthouseFriends gives 1899)
Mast light replaced by a wooden lighthouse tower. Work under way in the year to 30 June 1906; reported as finished in the report for the year to 31 March 1908. Rowlett and the Society give 1907.
Automated; battery system with a sun switch installed in October 1961
Moved southward to escape beach erosion
Commercial power connected to the light
Crown land under the light became Lennox Passage Provincial Park
Tower moved again, onto its present concrete foundation

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Department's report for the year to 30 June 1906 shows the tower under way; the report for the year to 31 March 1908 reports the replacement done. Rowlett and the Society give 1907, which falls in that span.

The 1908 report gives 32 feet (9.8 m) from base to lantern ventilator, and its 1909 changed-lights list calls the tower a 25-foot tower. The story states both; the report does not reconcile them. Lighthouse Directory gives 8.5 m (28 ft). The Coast Guard list gives a 9.2 m focal height and no tower height, so the earlier 9.5 m had no cited source and was replaced.

notes_for_editor: Dates for the tower disagree: the Department's reports show it under way in the year to 30 June 1906 and reported done in the year to 31 March 1908, while Rowlett and the Society say 1907. Heights disagree within the 1908 report (32 ft to ventilator; 25-foot tower in the changed-lights list) and across sources (Coast Guard 9.2 m focal height and no tower height; Rowlett 8.5 m tower and 9 m focal plane). The pole-light move is 1899 in LighthouseFriends; a Wikipedia article gives 1900 (not cited; the Department reports in the local corpus do not show it). Clough's salary is $60 in LighthouseFriends and $54 in Wikipedia (not cited). Charles J. Shannon: LighthouseFriends gives 1919 to at least 1923; Wikipedia gives Charles Shannon 1909 to 1923 (not cited). The keepers' statements in the corpus are OCR tables: the 'July 4, 1884' date (1901 report, printed p.129) and the 'Clough, Daniel Grand Digue Pole Light' row (1906 report, printed p.172) were checked on the page images, where the Clough row and the Grandique Pole Light entry sit on the same printed line, with the July date beside them; the 1909-1915 Kaulback entries (D. A. Kaulback Feb. 17, 1908; C. A. Kaulback Feb. 12, 1909) were not tied to this station in the OCR and are not used. The contractor's name is printed 'Lawrence Mury' in the 1908 report's OCR (prose, not a table; not checked on the page image) and in Wikipedia; LighthouseFriends prints 'Lawrence lIury' in its OCR-like text. 'Stanley Foregron' in one LighthouseFriends sentence is the same keeper as Forgeron. No wreck or rescue tied to this light was found in the corpus or the sources read; the 1923 Lennox Passage bridge incident is not tied to the light and is not used. Grande-Digue, New Brunswick, which appears in the Department's buoy lists, is a different place and is excluded. Stanley Forgeron and Melvin Shannon are named only in their keeper roles, as published sources name them. Newspaper search (Chronicling America) returned no hits for this station.
